title: Stalkwise flatness over the affine direct-image algebra
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be an affine morphism of schemes [pqf-def-affine-morphism, def-pc-scheme], and let $g:(X,O_X)\to(Y,f_*O_X)$ be the canonical ringed-space morphism [def-sc-direct-image-algebra-derived-category]. For every $x\in X$, the canonical stalk ring homomorphism $(f_*O_X)_{f(x)}\to O_{X,x}$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map].

source.place: Tag 0AVW, lemma-affine-morphism-equivalence, affine stalk calculation; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0AVW

proof.text: Choose an affine neighborhood U of f(x). Its inverse image is affine. Set A = Γ(X,f⁻¹U), S = (f_*O_X)_{f(x)}, T = O_{X,x}. The pushforward germ makes S the localization of A at the image of Γ(Y,U) minus the prime of f(x), by affine_pushforward_stalk_isLocalization.

The affine stalk theorem identifies T as a prime localization of A, so IsLocalization.flat gives Module.Flat A T. PresheafedSpace.stalkMap_germ for the canonical ringed-space map identifies the composite A → S → T with the germ A → T, giving IsScalarTower A S T. Module.flat_iff_of_isLocalization S M T then descends Module.Flat A T to Module.Flat S T, exactly the stated RingHom.Flat.
